transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Marta Rodriguez, Daniel Kim, Ravi Patel, Lena Novak, Tina Alvarez (Summit Retail)

Summary:
Quick closeout sync for Summit Retail pilot. Review of final results (latency, quality, cost), discuss tuning knobs, validate success criteria, agree next steps for production canary on Dedicated capacity and procurement path. Ask list: SOC2/KMS, network diagram, and exec recap.

Topics:
- Pilot results recap (latency, throughput, inference cost)
- Quality regressions / examples and eval sets
- Dedicated vs Hosted for production rollout
- Security/compliance gating (SOC 2, KMS, SSO)
- Next steps & timeline for canary and procurement

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick agenda — recap the pilot numbers, go over any open items, and align on next steps. we have about 45 minutes, so we'll try to be crisp.

[00:28] Marta (Summit): great, thanks Alex. overall excited to see the numbers you sent last night, quick comment — some of the labels in the csv were mangled so i didn't get all of them, but we can walk through.

[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): yep that was my export, sorry — i think the sequence id column got renamed in the pipeline, i'll re-upload a cleaned artifact after the call.

[01:12] Daniel (Summit): first question — latency numbers, your deck shows 95th pct at ~180ms on hosted; is that with prefix cache enabled?

[01:35] Priya: good Q. the hosted profile had prefix/KV cache on for repetitive queries; for cold starts it's more like 320ms 95th. on Dedicated we saw 95th ~120-140ms with the same workload, and sustained throughput was about 3x.

[02:10] Ravi (Summit): and cost delta? we need to justify moving to Dedicated.

[02:22] Alex: yes, high level — hosted was cheaper for low volume, approx $0.0035 per request unit in our pilot traffic, Dedicated estimated to be ~40% lower unit cost at our committed throughput because of batching and reserved GPU amortization. i'll send the per-token sheet.

[03:05] Marta: okay, can you share the assumptions? concurrency, average tokens?

[03:18] Alex: sure — pilot used median sequence 45 tokens, peak concurrency ~180, average throughput 60 requests/sec during business hours; i'll include the raw traces.

[04:00] Priya: also worth noting the quality tradeoff — we tested two quantization profiles; 8-bit gave negligible quality loss on our eval set but saved about 25% compute. we flagged one regression on the product naming prompts, that's in the QA examples doc.

[04:38] Marta: i saw that — the product-name hallucination on test vector #12. is that stable?

[04:48] Priya: it's repeatable when we use the smaller context window; increasing context length or using a rerank step fixes it. recommendation is rerank or slight prompt tweak.

[05:20] Daniel: from procurement's lens, we need clear SLAs and fallbacks — what happens if Dedicated goes down or we hit region capacity?

[05:36] Jordan (CSM): you can configure smart routing and automatic fallback to hosted model variants; we support canary and A/B routes so traffic will failover to hosted with a compatibility model. we'll add that to the runbook.

[06:10] Lena (Security): on compliance — we need SOC 2 report, network diagram, and confirmation of KMS support for keys. also SSO/SAML integration with Okta.

[06:29] Alex: all available — we'll share our SOC 2 report and a network diagram, and yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Okta SAML is supported, we have examples in the security pack.

[06:50] Lena: good. also, retention — what logs do you keep and for how long?

[07:02] Jordan: by default audit logs are 90 days in the console; we can arrange extended retention as an add-on for enterprise. request/response bodies are not stored for hosted by default; for Dedicated you control that in your cluster.

[07:30] Marta: success criteria — we defined earlier: 1) 95th percentile latency under 200ms for main flow, 2) <=1% quality regression on eval set, 3) cost per request within approved threshold. are we aligned that these were met?

[07:52] Priya: based on pilot metrics: latency meets criteria on Dedicated (95th ~120-140ms), quality regression measured 0.6% on our eval suite with the recommended quant profile and reranker, and cost projections within the threshold for committed volume.

[08:20] Ravi: that's promising. any outstanding technical risks we should be aware of?

[08:27] Priya: a couple: 1) cold-start latency for very bursty traffic — mitigations are warm-up hooks and prefilling KV cache, 2) model compatibility for a small subset of edge prompts — we suggest a small rerank service to handle those, 3) network egress constraints if you want on-prem variant.

[09:05] Marta: what's the canary plan look like? timeline?

[09:12] Jordan: propose a 2-week canary starting 2026-04-12 on Dedicated: week 1 limited to 10% traffic, week 2 ramp to 50% with close monitoring, and rollback rules if error rate or latency exceeds thresholds. we'll run synthetic loads and share dashboards.

[09:41] Tina (Procurement): procurement needs cost estimate and term sheet to start PO; can we get that by next week?

[09:50] Alex: yes we'll send an itemized cost spreadsheet and term options by 2026-04-09.

[10:05] Daniel: one more — did we compare with Anthropic or other vendors for this workload? I know you mentioned OpenAI and Google as references.

[10:18] Alex: we ran a light benchmark on Anthropic-ish models; main differentiator was throughput and cost at scale — Redwood Dedicated showed better sustained TPS for this model family. i'll include notes comparing our numbers with public benchmarks, but not a full apples-to-apples.

[11:02] Priya: linking artifacts: pilot-results-2026-04-06.xlsx, qa-examples.md, runbook-canary.md (we'll upload to the shared drive).

[11:25] Marta: thanks. on the exec summary — i'd like a one-pager that calls out business impact and TCO.

[11:33] Alex: we'll produce an exec one-pager and schedule a 30-min review with procurement + execs — propose 2026-04-14.

[12:00] Lena: small note on encryption — we need proof of key rotation policy and HSM attestations for legal.

[12:12] Jordan: we'll include the HSM attestation docs in the package.

[12:35] Ravi: for the technical closeout — can we get a follow-up SE deep-dive for our infra team to validate the ops hooks?

[12:45] Priya: yes, happy to run a 60-min deep dive next week; i'll propose two slots in calendar.

[13:05] Alex: ok, summary of next steps: final report and cost sheet by 4/9, docs (SOC2, network diagram, KMS) by 4/8, canary plan kick-off 4/12. if that all looks good we'll move to procurement.

[13:26] Marta: sounds good, i'm comfortable moving forward pending the one-pager and procurement sign-off.

[13:40] Tina: procurement will need the term sheet, send to procurement@summitretail.com.

[14:00] Alex: noted. any other blockers?

[14:07] (brief cross-talk)

[14:20] Daniel: no, thanks all.

[14:30] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the canary kick-off.

[44:30] Meeting end (manual end marker)

References / shared links mentioned:
- pilot-results-2026-04-06.xlsx (uploaded to drive)
- qa-examples.md (highlighted regressions)
- runbook-canary.md (canary/rollout plan)
- Security pack (SOC2, network diagrams, KMS integration examples)

End of transcript.
